newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi fails to appear at barricades.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi fails to appear at barricades.

text.p: Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi failed to appear on Saturday to address about 800 of her supporters who waited for more than an hour outside barricades blocking access to her house.
Members of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) gave no reason for the Nobel Peace laureate's failure to speak to her supporters, who dispersed peacefully.
On previous weekends she would drive outside the barricades in her car to speak for about five minutes to supporters before asking them to return home.

Suu Kyi's motorcade was attacked earlier this month by a crowd of stone-throwing, stick-wielding men believed to have been organised by the Union Solidarity and Development Association, a government-sponsored organisation.
The military government denied involvement in the incident but Suu Kyi and many diplomats said there was no doubt the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) orchestrated the attack.
Since late September, the government has been trying to stop Suu Kyi from giving regular weekend speeches to supporters from her front gates by blocking off access roads.
In Saturday's show of support for Suu Kyi, the crowd rallied near an intersection about two km (1.2 miles) from her home on University Avenue which was closed off to the public by police.

Supporters of Suu Kyi's NLD, which won a landslide election victory in 1990 but has never been allowed to rule, gathered under the watchful eyes of nearly 100 anti-riot police armed mostly with batons.

Burma's military leaders have faced international criticism for refusing to recognise the election results, causing problems for Rangoon's application for membership of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Saturday that ASEAN leaders agreed at a summit in Jakarta that Burma, Cambodia and Laos should join the seven-nation group simultaneously, but no date was set.
